notes: Demonstration assumptions for method discussion; the 60 s and 60 s values are not calibrated operational standards.
Every 5 s, the controller checks for any policy degradation inside the 60 s warning horizon.
When warned, all candidates are evaluated over one common 120 s interval: 60 s warning plus 60 s extension.
A candidate may take longer than 60 s but must finish within 120 s and pass the provisional curvature guard.
Candidate benefit is the reduction in integrated ordinal policy cost with l(C)=0, l(R)=1 and l(F)=2.
Among improving candidates, selection minimizes policy cost, then endpoint policy severity, displacement and maneuver duration.
Local grid only; singleton exposure with no neighboring traffic, ACC, three-dimensional conflict resolution or capacity estimate.
The controller is modular receding-horizon logic, not a calibrated MPC or multi-stage dynamic-programming optimum.
